cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul tells husbands, "Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them." (Colossians 3:19) Love them, and don't be harsh. It's a short instruction, friends, but I think it takes a whole lifetime to practice.

The answer is that it is pleasing to the Lord. Paul says, "Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord." (Colossians 3:20) His reason is the Lord's pleasure, plain and simple.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, "Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged." (Colossians 3:21) So he tells fathers not to provoke, and he names what's at stake: discouraged children. I think this one is a gentle word, and I know a little about how heavy discouragement feels after my years in that dark junk drawer.

The answer is while the masters are watching. Paul says to obey "…not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord." (Colossians 3:22) The point is a heart that stays the same whether anyone is looking or not. Every grown-up knows that pull.

The word is sincerity, friends. Paul wants obedience "…with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord." (Colossians 3:22) Sincerity means the heart matches what the hands are doing. It's like a cookie that's the same all the way through, not just frosted on top.

The answer is an inheritance! Paul says, "…you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward." (Colossians 3:24) An INHERITANCE. Not a pat on the back, not a coupon that expired in 2009, but an inheritance, and it comes from the Lord Himself.

The answer is False, friends. Paul doesn't say they are really serving their earthly masters. He says, "It is the Lord Christ you are serving." (Colossians 3:24) So the service ends up with the Lord Christ. That changes how everyday work looks.

The answer is False. Paul says, "Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism." (Colossians 3:25) So nobody gets favoritism. Nobody gets special treatment, and nobody skips the line. That includes everybody in the house.

The word is fair, friends. Paul says, "Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven." (Colossians 4:1) The masters answer to a Master too. Right and fair is how he says they should treat the people under them.

The answer is thankful. Paul says, "Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful…" (Colossians 4:2) So prayer comes with watching and thanking. I thank God every day for reaching into that drawer I was stuck in and calling me out, so this one's close to my heart.

The answer is a door for the word, friends. Paul asks them to pray "…that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ…" (Colossians 4:3) He's in chains, and he asks for a door for the word. I think that tells you what matters most to him.

The answer is True. Paul says he wants to proclaim the mystery of Christ, "…for which I am in chains." (Colossians 4:3) The mystery of Christ is the reason for the chains. And he still asks for prayer to proclaim it.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, "Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time." (Colossians 4:5) Nothing there says to stay away from anyone. He wants them to act wisely when they're around outsiders.

The answer is so they know how to answer everyone. Paul says, "Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone." (Colossians 4:6) Gracious words go with knowing how to answer. And he says everyone, not just the easy people.
